purpose: This medication is a birth control pill used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help with painful or irregular periods, acne, or endometriosis. Your doctor may recommend it for other hormone-related conditions as well.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — estrogen and progestin — that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. They stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month, thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm cannot easily reach an egg, and thin the lining of your uterus. Together, these effects make it very hard for pregnancy to occur.
common_side_effects: Some people notice nausea, breast tenderness, or headaches when they first start taking it — these often improve after the first few months. You might also experience spotting or light bleeding between periods, mood changes, or decreased sex drive. Some people notice bloating or mild weight changes.
warnings: This medication is not recommended if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as it can increase the risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. If you experience severe chest pain, sudden vision changes, severe headache, or leg pain and swelling, seek medical attention right away. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections.
typical_dosing: Most commonly, you take one pill every day at the same time each day. Depending on your pack, you may take 21 active hormone pills followed by 7 reminder pills, or a 28-day pack with active pills every day. Taking it at the same time each day helps it work best and reduces spotting. If you miss a pill, follow the instructions in your package or ask your pharmacist what to do.
